lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: constructing linear and exponential functions from data
lessonRef.title: Concept model C: constructing linear and exponential functions from data

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: 500 grows 4% per year. Model and value after 3 years?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Quantity A grows by 71 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
A stays ahead permanently because 71 is larger than 2.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 3100(0.87)^t, with t in years. What does 0.87 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $3100
the total value lost over the asset's life
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.87, meaning a 13% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (1, -9) and (4, 6). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 9, 36, 144, 576. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 4.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 4.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.

items.prompt: A population of 800 grows by 11% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 4 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 120 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
A stays ahead permanently because 120 is larger than 2.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2200(0.85)^t, with t in years. What does 2200 represent?
choices: the number of years until the asset is worthless
the total value lost over the asset's life
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.85, meaning a 15% annual loss
the value of the asset when it was new, $2200

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (5, -32) and (10, -72). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 18, 36, 72, 144. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 2.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 2.

items.prompt: A population of 1100 grows by 8% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 6 years, to the nearest whole number.
